brief: Five-theme GS flow note. Nasdaq breaks to new highs even as the median corporate diverges, lagging as higher rates squeeze SMEs and consumers, so headline strength masks weak breadth. GS sees upside if the rally broadens since EPS can still surprise despite high rates hurting the consumer. The curve has steepened, a healthier setup than front-end stress. Front-end call skew is bid as a hedge against a growth shock or a Fed pause, and higher long rates hurt parts of the economy without derailing growth if volatility stays calm. DeepSeeks fundraising shows the AI capital race continuing. Compute pricing stays robust because compute, gigawatts and power are short, and Nvidias B200/H200 pricing confirms that live, so GS stays bullish the hardware behind compute. Le Pens RN shadow budget faces a low bar since OATs already price in the election. Over 25bn euros a year in identified cuts would help credibility, though less funding for Brussels raises a separate EUR risk. GS tactically likes a surprise in Europe, banks and French risk. Bab el-Mandeb risk is rising as Saudi presses the Houthis, but Washington feels no urgency to deal before the midterms. The tail risk is escalation against energy infrastructure.
